newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's daughter makes public appearance.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's daughter makes public appearance.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, confined to hospital ahead of planned heart surgery, sent his younger daughter on Friday on one of her first solo public engagements on his behalf.

Tatyana Dyachenko, 36, who emerged as an influential member of Yeltsin's entourage earlier this year during his re-election campaign, flew to the southern city of Rostov to visit children hurt in a train-school bus crash at a level crossing on Thursday.
"Neither my father nor my mother could come, so they asked me to come here instead," a sombre Tatyana told doctors in the hospital where the survivors of the crash were being treated.
"This will remain a nightmare for these children for the rest of their lives," she said in remarks broadcast on primetime television news programmes.
Seventeen children were killed when a train hit their school bus at a level crossing on Thursday morning. Yeltsin has declared Saturday a day of national mourning.
Tatyana said Moscow was ready to provide anything necessary to help the injured children make a full recovery.
She played a key role in Yeltsin's election campaign, drawing comparisons with French President Jacques Chirac's daughter Claude.
Tatyana was credited with softening the president's tarnished image, making him more appealing to women voters.

Some political analysts say she was partly behind the removal in June of Alexander Korzhakov, Yeltsin's old friend and chief bodyguard, and that she now has a similar role to Korzhakov, controlling access to the president and acting as his confidant.

Tatyana had remained well in the background until the president's latest spell in hospital, but gave her first major television interview last Sunday, countering speculation Yeltsin was very ill by saying her father was following events closely.
"He reads newspapers and he knows everything they say about him," she told Russian Television.
Yeltsin's doctor said on Thursday that Tatyana and her elder sister Yelena visited their father every day.
Their mother Naina is also in the same hospital convalescing from a kidney operation last month.

Doctors said on Wednesday that Yeltsin, 65, was fit enough for a heart operation, but that surgery would be postponed for at least six weeks. The operation -- a relatively routine bypass operation -- will improve the blood supply to Yeltsin's heart.
